cull_test: if the extractor's consumer treats Assumption:/Constraint:/Rationale: identically at first render, collapse them to Rationale:/Rejected:/See: (DESIGN_SPEC.md, SY5 disposition)

Assumption.note: never appears in the real f1Brainz PR #733 corpus (0 of 6). No code path in render.py ever read this kind differently from Rationale or Constraint. Collapsed by this verdict: still a recognized keyword at extraction (remediation fix 2), aliased to Rationale at the emission site (extract.py:TAG_KIND_ALIAS) rather than retired -- a comment authored with this word still extracts and renders.

Constraint.note: 4 of 6 real f1Brainz PR #733 tags used this word -- the most common single kind in the only real corpus -- but AUTHOR popularity is not the cull test's question. The renderer (scripts/code_map/render.py:tag_lines) treats it identically to Rationale and Assumption: same section, same order, same format, no branch anywhere reads the kind to vary behavior. Collapsed by this verdict: still a recognized keyword at extraction (remediation fix 2), aliased to Rationale at the emission site rather than retired -- retiring it silently would have converted four real, working tags into inert prose with zero signal, which the remediation review flagged as the actual defect. Extraction now normalizes it to Rationale before the statement is ever stored.

Rationale.note: the survivor name -- both the shipped grammar's own word and the normalization target for Assumption:/Constraint:. scripts/code_map/render.py:tag_lines is the ONE code path rendering all three trial words identically; no consumer in this build branches on kind.

Rejected.note: NOT a collapse candidate. The cull test's own text (DESIGN_SPEC.md's SY5 disposition) scopes the collapse question to 'Assumption:/Constraint:/Rationale:' only -- Rejected: was never on trial. It encodes a structurally different fact than a positive rationale (a road not taken, not a reason taken), which is why the spec names it as one of the three survivors regardless of what this gate found about the other three.

See.note: NOT a collapse candidate, for the same reason as Rejected: excluded from the cull test's scope by the spec itself. A See: tag is a reference (a pointer to another symbol), not a flavor of explanation -- its 'text' field holds a target, not prose, even though it renders through the same tag_lines loop as the other two survivors.

reasoning: Applied honestly per the handoff's standard: the renderer was built first (scripts/code_map/render.py:tag_lines), and only then inspected for whether it needed to tell Assumption:/Constraint:/Rationale: apart. It does not -- one list comprehension formats every tag as f'{kind}: {text}' with zero conditional dispatch on the kind value, verified mechanically by an AST-walk test (tests/test_code_map.py:CommentTagRenderTests.test_comment_tags_render_path_carries_no_branch_on_kind, widened in remediation fix 3 to also catch dispatch-by-lookup and match statements, not just an explicit compare) that fails if tag_lines' own source ever varies its treatment on kind. No distinction was invented to dodge the test. Original build (0d1af801) implemented the collapse as RETIREMENT (TAG_START stopped recognizing Assumption:/Constraint: at all); a remediation review proved retirement was silent breakage on the only real corpus -- 4 of the 6 real f1Brainz PR #733 tags use Constraint:, and retiring it converts them from potentially-consumed to never-again-consumed with zero signal, the survival law's own failure condition. Remediation fix 2 reimplements the SAME verdict (collapse to Rationale) as an ALIAS instead: TAG_START recognizes all five words, and extract.py:TAG_KIND_ALIAS normalizes Assumption:/Constraint: to Rationale at the point a tag becomes a statement -- tag_lines stays exactly as branch-free as the cull test proved it, and every real, already-written tag stays visibly consumed. The real corpus's own shape (4 of 6 tags already converged on one word, Constraint:) is read as evidence the cull costs little to a NEW author choosing among the survivor words, not as a reason to keep every word recognized forever, and not as license to break existing authored text.

evidence.render_uniform_treatment: scripts/code_map/render.py:tag_lines -- one list comprehension, f"{t['kind']}: {t['text']}" for every tag regardless of kind; pinned by tests/test_code_map.py:CommentTagRenderTests.test_comment_tags_render_path_carries_no_branch_on_kind
evidence.real_corpus_shape: f1Brainz PR #733 (read-only reference, commit e3d6b542): 4 Constraint, 1 Rejected, 1 Rationale, 0 Assumption, 0 See, 0 authored slugs -- inspected via `git show`, not built into this repo's test suite (f1Brainz is read-only)
evidence.shipped_grammar: scripts/code_map/extract.py:TAG_START == r'^[ \t]*#[ \t]*(Assumption|Constraint|Rationale|Rejected|See):[ \t]*(.*)$' -- all five words are recognized at extraction
evidence.kind_normalization_site: scripts/code_map/extract.py:TAG_KIND_ALIAS, applied in Extractor.tag_check() at the emission call site -- one dict lookup, not a branch in the renderer

consequence: Future authors write Rationale: where grammar v0 would have offered Assumption: or Constraint: -- the survivor is the one word a new author needs to learn. A comment using either retired word still extracts and renders, normalized to Rationale: at emission -- there is no author-visible breakage and no silent loss of an already-written tag. This changes what every future author writes, not just what this build parses, so it is also surfaced as a decision candidate for confirmation beyond this gate (per the handoff's map-anchor note), not silently finalized here alone.
